acceptance_criteria.criterion: reloadStoreContext() re-reads stores.json and updates the module-level StoreRouter and MultiStoreManager singletons.
After calling reloadStoreContext(), getStoreRouter() returns the newly created router.
When stores.json is absent or schema-invalid, reloadStoreContext() returns null and sets legacy-mode context.
The StoreRouter is constructed with skipDirCreate: true during reload.

summary: Added reloadStoreContext() to store-context.ts — re-reads stores.json via loadStoresConfig(), constructs a fresh StoreRouter with skipDirCreate:true and a new MultiStoreManager, then calls setStoreContext() to update the module-level singletons. Returns the parsed StoresConfig or null for missing/malformed/schema-invalid config (restoring legacy mode). Added an optional configPath parameter to support test isolation without filesystem side-effects.
Changed the two type-only imports (StoreRouter, MultiStoreManager) to value imports to allow instantiation within the new function. Added imports for loadStoresConfig and the StoresConfig type.

Created tests/storage/store-context-reload.test.ts with 7 test cases covering: valid config reload (router switches to multi-store mode), getStoreRouter() reflecting the new instance, missing stores.json → null + legacy mode, malformed JSON → null + legacy mode, schema-invalid JSON → null + legacy mode, skipDirCreate verification (non-existent store directory is NOT auto-created). All 358 storage-layer tests pass.

comments.note: store-context.ts: The module-level JSDoc block at the top describes setStoreContext() as 'called exactly once per process startup', but reloadStoreContext() deliberately allows repeated calls. A brief note in the module-level comment to mention this is now intentional would avoid future confusion.

The configPath override parameter on reloadStoreContext() exists purely for test isolation. If this function is later exposed via a GUI API endpoint, callers must not be allowed to pass arbitrary paths — the parameter should be omitted from the public API surface and kept as an internal test hook only.

summary: All 4 ACs verified. 7 dedicated tests pass (store-context-reload.test.ts). Full storage regression suite: 358/358 tests pass across 15 files. TypeScript build: no errors. All edge cases (missing config, malformed JSON, schema-invalid JSON, skipDirCreate) covered by tests and behave correctly.

comments.note: No issues found. Code is clean and consistent. The configPath override is correctly scoped to tests and not exposed via any public API surface.

summary: Implementation is clean and correct. reloadStoreContext() is minimal, fail-safe (StoreRouter/MultiStoreManager constructors throw before setStoreContext() is called, leaving prior state intact), and fully satisfies all four ACs. Two stale JSDoc blocks describing single-startup semantics were corrected in-place (Fix-Forward). No blocking issues found.

comments.note: store-context.ts: Updated the module-level JSDoc block — replaced 'Set once per process startup via setStoreContext()' with language that reflects the hot-reload capability added by reloadStoreContext(). Purely a documentation correction; no behavioral change.

store-context.ts: Updated the setStoreContext() JSDoc — removed 'Must be called exactly once per process startup' which is now misleading. Replaced with 'Called once at process startup and again by reloadStoreContext() whenever stores.json changes at runtime.' Purely a documentation correction; no behavioral change.

[documentation-forward] The reloadStoreContext() @param configPath note says 'used in tests to inject a temporary config file' but does not explicitly warn callers that this parameter must NOT be exposed via any GUI API endpoint. Add a one-line warning to the JSDoc: 'Internal test hook — must not be forwarded from HTTP handlers or public API surfaces.' This makes the contract unambiguous for future contributors working on WP-004 store CRUD handlers.

No concurrency guard on reloadStoreContext(): two overlapping calls will race and the last writer wins. Acceptable for the GUI use case (user-triggered sequential config changes) but worth noting for any future high-frequency reload path.

notes: reloadStoreContext() is fully implemented and exported from store-context.ts. All four acceptance criteria met. WP-004 (CRUD store handlers) can import and call this function after any saveStoresConfig() write to hot-reload the context without a server restart. The function signature is: `reloadStoreContext(configPath?: string): Promise<StoresConfig | null>` — the configPath parameter is a test-only escape hatch and should not be surfaced to GUI callers.

All ACs met and tests pass. reloadStoreContext() is safe for Reviewer to assess. Note for Reviewer: the module JSDoc still says 'called exactly once per process startup' — this is now inaccurate since reloadStoreContext() allows repeated calls by design. Minor doc clarity improvement only, not a functional issue.
